title: Christos:
title_short: Christos · Young People at the Table
headline: In Cyprus, young people who had never met the other side now sit at the peace table, and it works.
story: Christos sits on a youth committee in Cyprus with members from both communities. Many of them had never met someone from the other community. In about a year it became one of the most successful trust-building steps on the island.
His lesson for Israel and Palestine: put young people directly in the negotiation, with real decisions, resources and a mandate. They will live in the island they build. Energetic and hopeful.
do: Open on frame 1 on “never in their life” with the hook text.
Keep his pace. He talks fast. Let lines breathe with a 6-frame pause between bites.

Use at most one line of committee detail.
Cover every trim with B-roll or a soft speech ramp.
dont: No text that takes a side on Cyprus or on Israel / Palestine.
Nothing that says “a conference is happening”.
No camera-shutter sounds. No choppy jump cuts.

transcript:
Auto-transcript of FX6_LVH_6364.MXF (Christos, Brussels, 15 Sep 2026). Times are mm:ss in the source file. All lines are Christos except the off-mic question before 04:06. The source labels 02:00 "Interviewer": it is Christos.
[00:12] So, you see, in Cyprus we are promoting the youth participation in decision-making process
[00:18] and then in peace-building process regarding the Cypriot problem in many, many ways.
[00:24] First of all, I am a member of the Technical Bicommunal Committee on Youth which is a trust-building
[00:29] measure which was agreed in 2025 Geneva meeting between the President of the Republic of Cyprus,
[00:35] the Turkish Cypriot leader, the guarantor states and the United Nations and it was advocated
[00:41] from the youth, from the civil society, from some international organizations and institutions
[00:47] and the European Union and the UN and finally they agreed to establish this committee.
[00:51] So, 16 members are appointed by the President of the Republic of Cyprus and 16 members by the Turkish Cypriot leader
[00:57] and as the committee and me myself as a member of the committee I am trying to bring young people of the island together
[01:06] and this is a unique example of young people participating within the peace process,
[01:11] within the framework of the United Nations and within the track 2, 1.5 and 1 of the peace process in Cyprus.
[01:23] The committee held meetings with, for example, High Representative and Vice President of the Commission Kayakalas
[01:28] last June here in Brussels and many, many else with the personal envoy, with the leaders and it is very successful.
[01:39] As well, I am working with more, let's say, not institutionalized, not institutional youth projects
[01:49] and ways of young people to participate. I am President of an independent student movement
[01:55] and also I was the youth delegate in respect of Cyprus to the Congress of the Council of Europe
[02:00] where we tried also to develop a peace initiative for our island about local and regional authorities and the young people.
[02:09] So, to implement the youth peace and security agenda in practice in Cyprus in many, many levels
[02:16] and what I think that could help and benefit the Israeli-Palestinian context from Cyprus
[02:24] is that we should try to involve young people directly to the negotiation process when it will start in Israel and Palestine.
[02:37] Okay, no conflict is the same, but we know that in Cyprus, such as in the Israeli-Palestinian context,
[02:48] young people are also traumatized, some of them are polarized, but it is very important to involve all of them
[02:57] not only to say their opinion, but also to make some decisions, to give funding to them, to do some activities
[03:06] with the mandate from their elected leaders and representatives, such as for the example of Cyprus.
[03:14] And this example could also be brought more broader. So, for example, I proposed to the EEAS, lastly, recently,
[03:23] to establish such a committee of young individuals, young leaders and give them the mandate to make peace actions
[03:31] from the name of the European Union for youth in different areas, for example, maybe also in Israel and Palestine on the European level.
[03:39] It will be a very great idea and initiative and I think that the Commission and the European External Action Service shall consider this,
[03:48] as well as another international organization, the Council of Europe, shall also try to consider this.
[04:06] Yes, sure. For example, I will tell you about the work of the Technical Committee on Youth.
[04:12] In a little bit more than one year of its existence, the Technical Committee on Youth was one of the most successful trust-building measures
[04:22] implemented in the Cypriot problem. We brought together many, many young individuals which maybe did not meet an individual
[04:30] from the opposite community, from the other community, never in their life. It was the first time we transferred our opinions,
[04:38] the opinions of young people to the leaders, created policy papers and lots of this and even met the EU High Representative
[04:48] for Foreign Policy and exchanged some opinions and things. So this is very beneficial because we are creating and it's the truth.
[04:58] We are creating this idea and it's the truth that young people want the solution of the Cypriot problem and they are going to live
[05:07] in the island that they will build. So these, by its own, are creating movement within the peace process
[05:16] and this could be also implemented in the Israeli-Palestinian context. For example, young people can start the movement
[05:25] and then the decision-makers and the politicians can catch it and then achieve some real progress because they have the, how you say,
[05:36] they have the responsibility before the next generations.
[05:46] Thank you.
